chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The market of the Muslims is like their Masjid, meaning when one precedes to the market, it is for him like the Masjid.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions (referring to the Shia scholars/narrators)
key_terms.سَبَقَ: To precede or be first to arrive

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the marketplace in Shia Islam according to the hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the sanctity of commercial spaces, noting that the marketplace holds a status akin to the mosque for the community. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that economic transactions, when conducted with integrity and proper intention, are acts of worship that sustain social cohesion. The comparison underscores the integration of the mundane and the sacred in daily Muslim life.
